detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Cloud networking logs via provider TA with the modular input for `aws:elb:accesslogs`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.13.1.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `elb_status_code` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=aws sourcetype=aws:elb:accesslogs.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:elb:accesslogs" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:elb:accesslogs"
| table _time elb_status_code target_status_code request_processing_time
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.13.10_cloud_network_load_balan_10"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:elb:accesslogs` in `index=aws` to detect cloud network load balancer target unhealthy. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `elb_status_code` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_13_10_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Cloud networking logs via provider TA and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
